# d2r-mobile-positioning.md — scope and boundaries

<!-- Generated by skill `init-dsh-project` v1.8 on 2026-10-26.
     This file answers **one class** of question: "is X ours or upstream's?" "Who is this for?".
     Its only update trigger: **the is / is-not line moved**. -->

> Why this page exists: this repo is a fork of a very active upstream. The most expensive
> mistake here is not a bug — it is doing upstream's job in our fork (a diverging copy of shared
> code that conflicts on every sync), or doing our job in upstream's files.

## 1. What it is

`d2r-mobile` (the `downsea/d2r-mobile` fork) is **a downstream fork of
[jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) whose job is to make the
HarmonyOS port run flawlessly on HarmonyOS PC (2in1) and HarmonyOS phones — install, import,
play, save, at a stable 60 fps, with touch, keyboard/mouse and gamepad input.**

So it must:

1. Produce **one HAP** that installs and runs on both target devices (PC `2in1` + phone), built on
   this host's Linux arm64 toolchain. Criterion: SOT metrics M1/M2.
2. Make the PC a first-class desktop target: keyboard + mouse control, windowed / full-screen /
   resizable window. Criterion: SOT metrics M5/M6.
3. Support a gamepad on both devices. Criterion: SOT metric M7.
4. Hold a measured 60 fps on both devices, and survive long sessions, fold / unfold,
   background / foreground and backup / restore without losing a save. Criterion: SOT
   metrics M3/M4/M8/M9.
5. Send every fix to shared code back upstream as a PR, so the fork's divergence stays at
   `dm/harmony/` + our docs.

## 2. What it is not (is-NOT)

| Not this | Then where is it |
|---|---|
| The iOS / macOS / tvOS / Android ports | Upstream `jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile` |
| The shared engine roadmap (rewriter, host, Vulkan layer, new game features / endgame modes) | Upstream; we contribute PRs when HarmonyOS needs a change |
| Player-facing docs (`README*.md`, `docs/HARMONYOS*.md`) | Upstream; our findings reach them as upstream PRs |
| A distributor of game content or of HAPs that embed it | Explicitly never (upstream CONTRIBUTING rule 1) |
| An AppGallery release | Explicitly not now: the game needs the player's own files; a store listing is a separate decision (ADR) |
| HarmonyOS tablets, wearables, TVs, other phones | Not claimed; a device enters scope only with a device in hand and a recorded run |
| Online / multiplayer | Never — upstream is offline-only |

## 3. Who uses it

| User | What they need | What they don't care about |
|---|---|---|
| The maintainer (downsea), playing on MateBook Pro S and Mate X5 | A build that installs over the top, keeps saves, plays like the PC game on the laptop and like a phone game on the phone | iOS / Android parity |
| Upstream maintainers and community | Clean, bilingual, single-purpose PRs for HarmonyOS fixes | Our doc surface, our metrics machinery |
| Agents working here | Clear "ours vs upstream" lines, device facts, a gate | — |

## 4. Boundary calls (how to use this page)

When a request lands on the boundary, ask in order:

1. Does it change **shared code** (`dm/host`, `dm/gfx`, `dm/android`, `dm/tools`, `dm/ios`)? → it
   is an **upstream PR** on a branch, not a commit on our `main` (ADR-0001).
2. Does it change a **stable contract** (import layout, error codes, pack fingerprint, signing
   identity)? → ADR here + upstream agreement.
3. Is it only reachable on HarmonyOS (`dm/harmony/`, `__OHOS__` blocks, PC-only behaviour)? → it
   is ours to build; still offered upstream once verified.

## 5. Known grey areas (written down, never silent)

| Area | How it is judged now | When to re-judge |
|---|---|---|
| Changes in `dm/harmony/` itself | Upstream owns the directory; we develop on PR branches and keep `main` equal to upstream there | If upstream declines a PC change we need → ADR on carrying a local patch |
| Desktop input mapping already in `dm/host/app_mac.m` | Reuse its key / mouse semantics; port, don't reinvent | If the Mac mapping proves wrong on a 2in1 touch laptop |
| Mate X5 API level | The HAP needs API 26; unverified on the X5 | First `oh device info` on the X5 (issue 007) |
